{{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|The Strun is a standard shotgun. Reliable, versatile and deadly.}} The '''Strun''' is a powerful shotgun that is the successor to the {{Weapon|Mk1-Strun}}. The Strun bears good damage per shot and decent [[status chance]], capable of killing most light enemies in a single shot. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|7,500}}. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. *Innate [[multishot]] of 12 pellets. *Reloads one shell at a time at a rate of 0.5 seconds per shell, which can be interrupted at any point, allowing for tactical reloading while in combat. **Reloading has a 0.5 second delay to start and a 0.25 second delay to end. **Since the weapon reloads one shell at a time, [[mods]] that increase magazine size would also mean spending more time reloading. {{Advantages|class=Shotgun| *Highest pellet count of all pellet shotguns. }} {{Disadvantages|class=Shotgun| *Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 60% from 12m to 25m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]). *Tied with {{Weapon|Mk1-Strun}} for the second slowest [[reload speed]] of all shotguns, after {{Weapon|Strun Wraith}}. }} {{WeaponComparison|Mk1-Strun}} {{WeaponComparison|Strun Wraith|header=n}} {{WeaponComparison|Strun Prime|header=n}} ==Acquisition== A built Strun can be purchased from the [[Market]] for {{cc|25,000}}. ==Notes== *Reload time is 0.75s + 0.5s per round, coming to 3.75 total seconds to reload a completely empty mag. **This time will further increase if magazine mods such as {{M|Ammo Stock}} are used. *Compared to the {{Weapon|Boar}}, the Strun has a tighter pellet cone and a much more efficient ammunition economy. The {{Weapon|Hek}} has an even smaller base magazine size than the Strun, but bears an even tighter pellet cone and a more efficient ammunition economy. The Strun could be considered the middle ground of the three. *Before {{ver|12}}, the weapon's price in the market was {{cc|75,000}}. ==Incarnon Genesis== {{Transclude|Strun Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}} {{Transclude|Strun Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}} ==Tips== *Using {{M|Shotgun Ammo Mutation}} or {{M|Vigilante Supplies}} can help regain ammo when needed, although not as often as the full auto shotguns. *Weapon's spread cone can be shrunk by zooming in. ==Trivia== *The Strun appears to use a tubular magazine, presumably the cylindrical protrusion near the rear above the stock - the Warframe will push this section while reloading. **Assuming the Warframe is adding shells into this tube, or replacing it, it would imply that the shells used by Strun are extremely small, which is puzzling given the enormous choke. *When it was originally released, the Strun was magazine-fed, with the small knob on top of the weapon being its magazine. This was changed into the shell-feed system currently in use. *The regular Grineer [[Trooper]] previously used this weapon prior to {{ver|11}}, and currently wield {{Weapon|Sobek}}s. *[[Corrupted Crewman|Corrupted Crewmen]] used to wield a Strun in Void missions, except their version fired a burst of yellow energy pellets instead of bullets. *The Strun shares many similarities to the Boar. *The Strun received a PBR (Physically Based Rendering) update in {{ver|16.7}}. ==Media== Strun (1).png|Strun when equipped in the arsenal Strun (2).png Strun (3).png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|Uub7Mjer8nk|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|6zY3TOlnq7k|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|37.0.1}} *Fixed the Strun clipping into Koumei when holstered. {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Strun {{ver|30.9}} *Fixed reloading an extra bullet into the Strun if you fired 5 or more shots before the reload. {{ver|27.2}} ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. *(Undocumented) Status chance per projectile increased from {{#expr: 20/12}}% to 5%. {{ver|17}}
Several changes have been made to shotgun weapons across the board -- resulting in a list of changes similar from weapon to weapon. The following list of changes apply to all Primary Shotguns with exception to the Phage: *Increased damage across all shotguns. *Damage after projectile falloff has been increased for all shotguns. *Some shotguns have been given improvements to reload speed. *Some shotguns have received improvements to their projectile speed. *Death at close to mid range will now toss enemies into a forceful ragdoll. *(Undocumented) Strun series changed from magazine-based reload to shell-by-shell reload. {{ver|7.10}} *Effective range increased. {{ver|7.x}} *Tweaks to Recoil feel and Accuracy, generally sharper Rotation and Translation Springs, added Noise & better spread control when firing while aimed. Added force feedback to all firing sounds. *Increased damage per pellet from 12 to 14. *Decreased reload time from 3.37 to 3. *Increased Crit Chance from 5% to 7.5% {{ver|Vanilla}} *Introduced with game release. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Mk1-Strun}}, the [[Mk1]] counterpart of this Weapon. *{{Weapon|Strun Prime}}, the [[Prime]] variant of this Weapon. *{{Weapon|Strun Wraith}}, the [[Wraith]] counterpart of this Weapon. *[[Strun Incarnon Genesis]], the Incarnon power-up for the Strun series. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Strun]] [[es:Strun]] [[fr:Strun]] [[Category:Shotgun]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Tenno]] [[Category:Closed Beta]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Impact Damage Weapons]] [[uk:Стран]] [[Category:Weapons Purchasable For Credits]] [[Category:Vanilla]]

{{ModBox}}
'''Stunning Speed''' is a [[mod]] that increases [[reload speed]] and [[status chance]] by 10% and 7.5% per rank for a maximum of 40% and 30%, respectively.

==Stats==
{| class="emodtable"
|-
! [[Mod#Mod Rank|Rank]]
! [[Reload speed]]
! [[Status chance]]
! [[Mod#Attributes|Cost]]
|-  
| 0 || +10% || +7.5% || 6
|-
| 1 || +20% || +15% || 7
|-
| 2 || +30% || +22.5% || 8
|-
| 3 || +40% || +30% || 9
|}

==Drop Locations==
{{DropLocations}}

==Notes==
*'''Stunning Speed''' is additive with similar mods. For example, a {{Weapon|Sicarus}} with a max rank '''Stunning Speed''' and {{M|Sure Shot}} will have a {{Math|6% {{mul}} (1 + 30% + 90%)|t = y|p = y}} status chance.
*This mod doesn't directly reduce reload times; it increases reload speed. The calculations are far different, and that can cause some confusion.
**The calculation of reload time using reload speed as a variable is almost the same with melee charge speed, which is ''Base Reload Time{{div}}(1+ Reload Speed Bonus)''.
**The 40% reload speed bonus at max rank equates to a ~29% reduction to reload times. You can calculate the reduction as 1-(1{{div}}(1+s)), where s is your total reload speed bonus.
*Stacking this with {{M|Quickdraw}} should reduce reload times by 47%.

{{Top|Lotus|Tenno|Tenno|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|A different take on a familiar shotgun, the Strun Wraith features unique styling.}} The '''Strun Wraith''' is the first [[Wraith]] weapon and a variant of the {{Weapon|Strun}} with overall improvements, including significantly higher [[status chance]]. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals primarily {{D|Impact}} damage. *Shots have a forced enemy [[stagger]]. *Innate [[multishot]] of 10 pellets. *Reloads one shell at a time at a rate of 0.45 seconds per shell, which can be interrupted at any point, allowing for tactical reloading. **Reloading has a 0.25 second delay to start and a 0.25 second delay to finish. **The reload time is increased indirectly if magazine increasing mods are equipped. *Innate {{Pol|Naramon}} polarity. {{Advantages|class=Shotgun|}} {{Disadvantages|class=Shotgun| *Has linear damage falloff from 100% to 50% from 15m to 30m target distance (distances are affected by [[Projectile Speed]]). *Slowest [[reload speed]] of all shotguns. }} {{WeaponComparison|Mk1-Strun}} {{WeaponComparison|Strun|header=n}} {{WeaponComparison|Strun Prime|header=n}} ==Acquisition== This weapon was first introduced from the [[Survival Weekend Event]], awarded for completing the event's [[Survival]] for 20 minutes, complete with a free weapon slot and a pre-installed [[Orokin Catalyst]]. The Strun Wraith was awarded again from acquiring 100 points in the [[Tactical Alert#Den of Kubrow|Den of Kubrow Tactical Alert]], also complete with a free weapon slot and a pre-installed Orokin Catalyst. The blueprint and parts were formerly a reward from the [[Sortie/ArchivedRewards|Fourth Season]] of [[Sortie]]s; they can now be found as an [[Invasion]] reward. All components can be [[Trade System|traded]], although players must have a [[Mastery Rank]] of at least 10 to acquire the blueprint. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Incarnon Genesis== {{Transclude|Strun Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}} {{Transclude|Strun Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}} ==Tips== *Strun Wraith combines well with [[critical chance]] and [[critical multiplier]] mods. *A high [[status chance]] build can provide significant benefits to the weapon's performance. *Although reloading the entire magazine is slow, the weapon can be reloaded as needed immediately after firing, and can be fired in the middle of reloading to interrupt the process. Clever management of reloading in between combat will greatly assist with the slow reload. Bullet jumping will not interrupt the reload. ==Trivia== *When the Strun Wraith was first released, it had a [[critical chance]] of 50%, making it the weapon with the highest [[critical chance]] (prior to the release of the {{Weapon|Synapse}}). This was unintended and was changed in {{ver|9.7.3}} a few hours after release. *This weapon was a reward for surviving at least 20 minutes during the Survival Weekend Event in a single round. *The Strun Wraith is the first [[Wraith]] [[Tenno]] weapon. *The Strun Wraith is the first Wraith weapon to be re-released. *As with many other old Wraith and [[Vandal]] weapons, only the energy color could be changed. Other colors may be selected, but would not show on the weapon unless said weapon possessed a skin. ** As of {{ver|22}}, all default skins of Vandal and Wraith weapons can be fully colored. This includes the Rakta Syandana. ==Media== StrunWraithCodex.png|Strun Wraith in Codex. Strun Wraith (1).png|Strun Wraith as shown in the Arsenal Strun Wraith (2).png {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|vo2cPG8505w|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|_bc5tL48Wu8|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|G42GanRbyOQ|size=300px}} }} {{SkinGallery}} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|38.5.10}} *Fixed the Strun Wraith missing its recoil stat for its Incarnon Form (when it has an Incarnon Adapter installed). **Also fixed it using the default Strun Wraith icon if it had an Incarnon Adapter installed. {{ver|32.3.3}} *Fixed the Strun Wraith unintentionally having its’ critical chance increased to 38% (returned to the prior value of 18%). {{ver|32}} ;Ammo Changes We understand the power fantasy of these weapons is very popular for some, so our first approach was to keep them powerful, but limit how often they can be used by making changes to ammo pick-up. '''''Ammo Pickup Overrides'''''
The following weapons now have ammo pickup overrides, meaning they gain less from picking up ammo. This mostly applies to AoE weapons, in hopes that players will become more deliberate with their aim to make the most of their Ammo pools. The following lists the specific ammo pick up overrides per weapon category. '''Primary Weapon Ammo Pick Up Overrides''' 15 Ammo per Pick Up: *Strun Wraith {{ver|27.2}} ;Greater than 100% Status having meaning: Shotguns have a unique Role here based on a very patch-work history with how they interact with Status Chance. A Shotgun that shoots 99% Status Chance would give you 35% (roughly) status per pellet. 100% Status Gives you 100% Status per pellet. This huge jump in performance happens with just a 1% gain - why? Well, to answer that we have to look at our choice to make what the UI conveys reality. It would feel broken to shoot a Shotgun with 100% Status and not see a perfect spread of Effects. In reality, to make Status consistent we have to treat Shotguns as a special case. Shotguns as a special case means we have buffed the Status Chance of all Shotguns by x3 or greater. The UI now behaves to show the reality that you are determining Status Chance per pellet. *(Undocumented) Status chance per projectile increased from 4% to 12%. {{ver|22.12}} *Mastery Rank increased from 0 to 10. *Damage increased from 30 to 40 (per pellet). *Critical chance increased from 15 to 18%. *Critical Damage from 2 to 2.2x. {{ver|18.4.5}} *Increased Ammo Magazine Capacity from 8 to 10. *Increased Slash Damage from 50 to 60. *Increased Puncture Damage from 37.5 to 45. *Increased Impact Damage from 162.6 to 195. *As a result of adding 2 more shots per Magazine, reload time for a full reload has slightly increased. *Added knockback and impulse to landed shots on enemies. {{ver|17}}

The following list of changes apply to all Primary Shotguns with exception to the Phage: *Increased damage across all shotguns. *Damage after projectile falloff has been increased for all shotguns. *Some shotguns have been given improvements to reload speed. *Some shotguns have received improvements to their projectile speed. *Death at close to mid range will now toss enemies into a forceful ragdoll. *(Undocumented) Strun series changed from magazine-based reload to shell-by-shell reload. }} ==See also== *{{Weapon|Strun}}, the normal counterpart of this Weapon. *{{Weapon|Mk1-Strun}}, the [[Mk1]] counterpart of this Weapon. *{{Weapon|Strun Prime}}, the [[Prime]] variant of this Weapon. *[[Wraith]], the special prefix of the Weapon. *[[Strun Incarnon Genesis]], the Incarnon power-up for the Strun series. {{WeaponNav}} [[de:Strun Wraith]] [[es:Strun Fantasma]] [[fr:Strun Wraith]] [[ru:Стран Призрак]] [[Category:Weapons]] [[Category:Primary Weapons]] [[Category:Shotgun]] [[Category:Wraith]] [[Category:Event Reward]] [[Category:Tenno]] [[Category:Update 9]] [[Category:Impact Damage Weapons]] [[Category:Tactical Alert Reward]] [[Category:Invasion Reward]] [[uk:Стран-примара]] [[Category:Invasion Weapons]]

{{Top|Enemy|Grineer|Grineer|Weapon|Weapons|Weapons}} {{WeaponInfoboxAutomatic}} {{Codex|Firing a sticky, toxic, explosive compound, the Stug Gel Gun offers multiple ejection modes, delivering maximum damage in all situations.}} The '''Stug''' is an automatic Grineer pistol that fires {{D|Corrosive}} blobs that stick to surfaces and explode. A larger and more powerful blob can be formed using consecutive automatic shots or a single charged shot via [[Alternate Fire]]. This weapon can be sold for {{cc|5,000}}. ==Characteristics== *This weapon deals '''100%''' {{D|Corrosive}} damage. *Fires blobs that stick to surfaces or embed into enemies, with a lifespan of '''1.5''' seconds. Blobs can be stacked by consecutively shooting one spot, refreshing the blob duration with each new stack added. After reaching '''10''' stacks or the lifespan running out, the blob will detonate and deal '''75 - 750''' damage in a '''0.3 - 2.8''' meter radius, scaling with the number of stacks. Explosion has '''70%''' damage falloff (despite being listed as '''30%'''), dealing '''30%''' damage at the edge of its radius. ** [[Multishot]] will not shoot additional blobs, but will instead shoot blobs with an equivalent amount of extra stacks. For example, '''+100%''' multishot will cause each blob shot to have '''2''' stacks, reaching max stacks after only '''5''' consecutive shots. ** Explosions do not [[Stagger|self-stagger]]. ** Explosion does not need direct [[Line of Sight]] to deal damage and will penetrate walls. ** Can benefit from {{M|Fulmination}} ({{M|Primed Fulmination|Primed}}). * While stuck to a surface, blobs deal '''4 - 36''' damage in a '''2''' meter radius, once immediately upon the blob embedding and then again every second. Damage scales with the number of blob stacks and has '''100%''' damage falloff, dealing '''0%''' damage at the edge of its radius. ** Extending the lifespan of a blob by adding stacks to it will allow it to continue dealing this AoE embed damage until the blob finally expires or reaches max stacks. * [[Alternate Fire]] charges up a fully ('''10''') stacked blob over '''2''' seconds, at the cost of '''10''' ammo. ** The alternate fire becomes unavailable while the [[Incarnon|Incarnon Adapter]] is installed in the weapon. *Innate {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarity. {{Advantages|}} {{Disadvantages| *Blobs have travel time with heavy arcing. *Low [[status chance]] on explosion. *Slow alt-fire charge rate. *Explosion has a [[Enemy Body Parts|headshot]] multiplier of '''1x''' and cannot trigger headshot conditions. *Explosion has linear [[Damage Falloff]] from '''100%''' to '''30%''' from central impact. *Damage over time has linear damage falloff from '''100%''' to '''0%''' from central impact. }} ==Acquisition== The Stug's blueprint can be purchased from the [[Market]]. {{BuildAutomatic|type=Weapon}} ==Notes== * Blobs can be stuck to allies. * Blobs will bounce off of [[Nullifier Crewman]] shields. ==Incarnon Genesis== {{Transclude|Stug Incarnon Genesis#Acquisition}} {{Transclude|Stug Incarnon Genesis#Incarnon Genesis}} ==Tips== *{{M|Barrel Diffusion}} and {{M|Lethal Torrent}} will allow the Stug to build up blobs much faster, while Lethal Torrent can increase firing and charging speed of the weapon. *{{M|Fulmination}} increases the crowd control potential of this weapon, particularly when spreading small blobs all over a room to deal damage against a large crowd of enemies. *The Stug can have three unique combination elementals, with Corrosive already provided, allowing Pathogen Rounds and {{M|Convulsion}} mods to be equipped separately for such combinations. *The Stug's shots will not just stick to enemies, but other players too. This lets you put them on another player for a little bit of quick melee defense (similar to Vauban's Teslas, but much shorter-lived). Also, the shots will stick to Loki's Decoy and Saryn's Molt for an effective trap. *The innate {{Pol|Vazarin}} polarity can somewhat limit elemental modding potential unless building for {{D|Magnetic}}, {{D|Blast}} or {{D|Viral}} damage, thus making it a less desirable polarity for elemental modding. If you wish to focus more on different elemental damages, then it is recommended to either ignore the polarity or use [[Forma]] to turn it into a more suitable polarity. ==Bugs== * Despite the UI listing the weapon's radial damage falloff as only '''30%''' (dealing 100% - 70% damage over its range), it is actually '''70%''' (dealing 100% - 30% damage over its range), dealing far less damage than intended. ==Trivia== *The Stug is the third of four very large secondary weapons, the first two being the {{Weapon|Acrid}} and the {{Weapon|Ballistica}}, with the {{Weapon|Sepulcrum}} being the fourth. *"''Stug''" is likely taken from the WW2 German assault gun of the same name ([[wikipedia:Sturmgeschütz III|Sturmgeschütz III]] & [[wikipedia:Sturmgeschütz IV|IV]]); this makes it the second Grineer weapon named after a military vehicle, the first being the {{Weapon|Hind}}. *This is the second secondary weapon that has a Charge ability. *While the game startup window (the one that lists recent updates) refers to the Stug as a Goo-gun, the shop calls it a Gel gun. *Stug blobs that embed onto the [[Jackal]] are unable to deal damage to it. *The weapon strongly resembles the ''[https://unreal.fandom.com/wiki/Bio_Rifle Bio Rifle]'' in Digital Extremes' 1999 game ''Unreal Tournament''. Both weapons fire short-range, slow-moving arcing blobs that stick to surfaces, and both weapons have rapid autofiring as primary fire, and the alternate fire charges a larger blob. While Stug fires white blobs with corrosive damage, the Bio Rifle fires globs of green toxic sludge. ==Media== StugCodex.png|Stug in Codex. {{VideoGallery |{{YouTube|ng1c8PHnZvs|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|Zph70C5sQTY|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|nl4aNfjpW9A|size=300px}} |{{YouTube|BoT1gPJVbI4|size=300px}} }} ==Patch History== {{Scrollbox/Article| {{ver|43.0.4}} *Fixed various issues with Stug's stats in the Upgrade Screen: **Critical Chance, Radial Status Chance, and Status Chance always displaying as 0%. **Blob Embed Damage causing Elemental Damage to appear twice for Quick Shot stats. {{ver|43.0.1}} *Increased the Stug's Blob Embed Status Chance to 10%. {{ver|43}} *Updated the Stug to improve ease of use with the following changes: **Projectiles have improved stacking collision to make stacking easier. **Blobs which reach 10 stacks now immediately explode. **Improved the charge speed of the Alt Fire and increased the number of stacks shot at maximum charge (Now 10, from 6). **Updated the visuals of the projectiles and projectile explosions. {{ver|32}} ;Headshot Damage Changes During playtesting, the ammo changes alone weren’t enough to significantly change things for AoE weapons. So instead of tightening these values to be overly restrictive, we chose to address other factors that make these weapons so strong, such as headshot damage. Our approach here is two-fold, to reduce the impact of headshots for AOE weapons, but to also make precision headshots pack a larger punch overall. *Radial damage no longer gains extra headshot damage or triggers headshot conditions. **This is primarily targeted at the Ignis Wraith - as a “flamethrower” weapon, it’s hard to imagine a blanket of elements being precise enough to target weak points specifically. Explosive projectiles themselves can still land headshots, so there is still a reason to aim with most weapons for maximum damage. {{ver|28.3}} *Fixed the Stug’s alt-fire doing self-damage. {{ver|27.2.2}}
Reduced the following AoE weapons Radial Damage Falloff from central impact that were all previously 90%: *Stug: 30% {{ver|27.2}} ;Self Damage Changes: We are getting rid of Self Damage and replacing it with something else: instead of Self Damage, it’s now ‘Stagger’. This change completely removes the chance of killing yourself, and instead now creates scenarios where you will interrupt yourself - or ‘Stagger’ - to varying degrees if you aren’t careful. The degrees of Self-Interrupt start with a small stumble all the way to full knockdown depending on how close you are to the center of explosion. Any Mods referring to Self Damage will be converted to acknowledge Stagger. With this Self-Interrupt system, we have added dozens of new recovery animations that harness a ninja-like recovery experience. By pressing ‘Jump’ at the correct time, you can execute a ninja-skill-based knockdown recovery to ALL in-game knockdowns. This ninja recovery window is indicated by a glowing FX on your Warframe. In the original Dev Workshop, we said:
''As a result of this overall systemic change, Weapons with Stagger will be getting approximately a 20% buff in Damage, with any weapons with AOE receiving a 50% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact.'' This is no longer accurate after continued testing. What we are doing now is: No damage buffs have been added, but any weapons with AOE are receiving ~20% increase in Radius. Additionally, AOE weapons are receiving a 90% Radial Damage Falloff from central impact. This means on the very outer section of the explosion Radius 10% of the Damage will be dealt. Tactics will be deadly - aim true, Tenno. ''Why: Several players brought up the history of the Tonkor and we want to make sure we ship this change in a place that’s conservative in its starting point from a balance perspective. The complete removal of Self Damage does change the pace of destruction with some of the game’s most powerful weapons, so we want to make sure we can iterate upwardly instead of releasing a bonanza of explosions with no other choices.'' {{ver|24.5.6}} *Fixed the camera momentarily being jerked forward when shooting the Stug at certain angles. {{ver|24.2.10}} *Fixed the Stug's projectiles interacting physically with ragdolls. {{ver|22.17.3}} *Fixed the Stug blowing up in your face when it is used with Mirage’s Hall of Mirrors. {{ver|18.8}} *Tweaked the Stug and Simulor projectiles to properly appear stacked instead of hovering over each other. '''Stug Incarnon Genesis''' is an item that is used to add [[Incarnon]] upgrades to the {{Weapon|Stug}}.

==Acquisition==
*Upon completion of [[The Duviri Paradox]] and [[Angels of the Zariman]], and unlocking [[The Steel Path]], players can earn {{Resource|Stug Incarnon Genesis}} from [[The Circuit]]'s Steel Path to place on their Stug with the help of [[Cavalero]] in the [[Chrysalith]]. This [[Incarnon Genesis]] form grants it evolutions to a transformation and newfound strength.
*Purchased from Cavalero for {{pc|120}}, complete with the resources used in its installation. This purchase can only be made '''once'''.

==Incarnon Genesis==
*Installing the {{PAGENAME}} requires 20 {{Resource|Pathos Clamp|Pathos Clamps}}, 150 {{Resource|Aggristone|Aggristone}}, and 60 {{Resource|Tasoma Extract|Tasoma Extract}}.
*When installed, the first Evolution tier is unlocked. The following Evolution tiers, their requirements for unlocking them, and their related perks, are shown below;
**Each challenge additionally grants '''5,000''' [[affinity]] to the weapon, affected by [[Affinity Booster]]s.

===Overview===
*Incarnon Form is charged by filling the Incarnon Transmutation gauge that appears under the reticle by hitting enemies with direct hits and then pressing the [[Alternate Fire]] button. '''30''' direct hits will completely fill the gauge. A full gauge is not required to activate Incarnon Form.
** '''1''' Incarnon charge is given on direct hit. '''1''' charge is given when a blob explodes, but only if the blob is attached to an enemy (charge is only given from the attached target, not surrounding enemies hit by the explosion). '''0''' charge is given from the embed DoT damage.
*** Once an enemy is killed, leftover blobs stuck to them will not give charge when they explode.
** Shooting additional blobs onto a blob that's already attached to an enemy will still grant '''1''' charge for each direct hit. However, only '''1''' ''total'' charge will be given for the final blob explosion, regardless of how many blobs are combined.
*** Because of this, Incarnon charge can be built faster by spreading out shots rather than stacking blobs in one spot. This will allow every shot to grant '''2''' charges; '''1''' from the direct hit and '''1''' from the explosion.
*** [[Multishot]] increases blob size rather than the number of blobs, so it does '''not''' increase the number of Incarnon charges gained per blob.
*Mode switching is '''not''' instantaneous and has an animation equal to the weapon's [[reload speed]].
*Swapping to and from Incarnon Form will fully reload the normal form's magazine.
*Instead of drawing ammunition from its reserves, the Stug's Incarnon Form uses a separate "magazine" with each charge producing '''4''' rounds to a maximum of '''120'''. Once all ammunition is expended, the Stug reverts to its normal form.
**Incarnon Form's magazine is '''not''' affected by mods.
**Incarnon Form is '''not''' affected by [[Ammo Efficiency]] (such as {{A|Energized Munitions}}).
**Charges and Incarnon Form persists through all activities, such as holstering, [[bleedout]], or being [[disarm]]ed. However, charges and Incarnon Form are removed upon [[death]].
